title: AMIP 1.1.9 monthly SST retains the 2018 Southern Ocean cold step in NOAA OI v2
abstract: We tested whether a reported 2018 cold step in NOAA OI SST v2 reaches PCMDI-AMIP monthly SST. We read AMIP 1.1.9 and 1.1.3, OI v2, ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2 on a fixed ocean mask. At 40-60 S, AMIP minus OI v2 varies by only 0.00034 C. The June 2018 AMIP step is -0.153 C against ERSSTv5 and -0.072 C against COBE-SST2. Both intervals stay below zero across three dates and three block lengths. Warmer fixed masks keep negative point estimates. At 50-60 S, removal of the June difference step changes the 2001-2022 trend point estimate from -0.029 to +0.007 or +0.051 C per decade. Relative cooling against the 60 S to 60 N mean is reduced by 27 to 52 percent. All 12.9 million tested cell-month values in the overlap of AMIP 1.1.3 and 1.1.9 are equal. Global and east-Pacific step estimates are unresolved. We test monthly observations, not adjusted boundary values or model radiation. Reference errors, a fixed step model and conditional uncertainty limit attribution. This establishes transfer of the feature to the AMIP monthly target, not its full physical cause or a feedback bias.

display.caption: Regional AMIP differences against two in situ references, and the small AMIP minus OI v2 residual. Anomalies use 1991-2010.
2001-2022 point trend sensitivity to removal of the June 2018 reference-difference step. Bars are diagnostic estimates, not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Tests whether its reported OI v2 step appears in the actual AMIP monthly release. Uses its reported step date but no extracted data or code.
